question: Ibn Battuta, a famous Moroccan traveller visited India during the time of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi Sultanate**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ibn Battuta**, a famous Moroccan traveller, visited India during the time of the **Delhi Sultanate**.
 
• The Delhi Sultanate was a period of Muslim rule in India that lasted from 1206 to 1526 AD.
 
• Ibn Battuta arrived in India in 1334 AD during the reign of Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
 
• He served as a judge (Qadi) in the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq for several years.
 
• Ibn Battuta's accounts provide valuable insights into the culture, politics, and society of India during the 14th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ibn Battuta** was born on February 25, 1304, in Tangier, Morocco.
 
• His travels are documented in his travelogue known as the **Rihla** (The Journey), which covers his journeys across Africa, Asia, and Europe over a period of almost 30 years.
 
• During his travels, Ibn Battuta visited many regions including North Africa, the Horn of Africa, West Africa, Southern Europe, Eastern Europe, the Middle East, South Asia, Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and China.
 
• His travel accounts are considered one of the most comprehensive sources of information about the medieval world.
 
• Ibn Battuta's journey to India was part of his larger quest to explore the Islamic world and beyond.
